Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (VP of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and David Kwon, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Ramirez.

John Ramirez (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Global Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s performance for the second quarter of 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, even as we navigate a complex macroeconomic environment marked by inflationary pressures and supply chain adjustments in our core manufacturing and industrial equipment markets. Let me highlight a few key achievements that underscore our resilience and strategic execution.

First, our aftermarket parts and services business delivered exceptional growth, reaching double-digit increases for the 11th straight quarter and now comprising a larger share of total revenue, providing high-margin stability amid softer new equipment demand. Second, we made substantial progress on our share repurchase program, executing opportunistically to retire millions of shares and enhance shareholder value. Third, our automation and digital offerings continued to accelerate, driving efficiency gains for customers and expanding our segment's contribution to the top line with impressive margin uplift. Fourth, revenue performance was strong across geographies, with notable outperformance in North America and Asia-Pacific offsetting softer spots elsewhere. Fifth, operating margins improved meaningfully in each of our key segments, reflecting better mix, pricing discipline, and cost controls. And sixth, our dividend policy remains a pillar of our capital returns, with a competitive yield supported by robust free cash flow generation.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives—from advancing Industry 4.0 solutions to strengthening our aftermarket footprint—are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth in the industrial equipment landscape.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, John. Turning to our financial performance, Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. reported $1.22 billion in revenue for the second quarter, representing a 13% increase year-over-year and 6% sequentially. This top-line strength was broad-based, with aftermarket services and digital solutions leading the way. Gross margin expanded 220 basis points to 42%, driven primarily by the higher mix from our high-margin aftermarket parts and services, as well as pricing actions averaging 3.5% across the portfolio and efficiencies from our lean manufacturing programs. Operating expenses were controlled at $285 million, resulting in operating income of $248 million. Our net income for the quarter was $162 million, or $1.45 per diluted share, surpassing our guidance and reflecting $0.12 of EPS accretion from our capital returns activities.

Let me start by diving deeper into our aftermarket parts and services business, which continues to be the crown jewel of our P&L—delivering high-margin, recurring revenue that anchors our overall performance amid the cyclicality of new equipment sales. In Q2, aftermarket parts and services revenue reached $452 million, up 16% year-over-year and 5% sequentially from Q1. This outpaced the broader industrial MRO market, which grew around 8-10% globally according to recent Gardner Intelligence data. As a result, aftermarket now represents 38% of our total revenue—up from 35% a year ago and 32% two years back. This shift stems directly from our multi-year ServiceMax strategy, executed relentlessly since 2021.

Breaking it down, parts revenue, which accounts for 62% of the aftermarket mix at $280 million, grew 18% YoY, driven by robust demand for high-wear components like hydraulic cylinders, conveyor belts, and precision gears in our core excavator lines, CNC machining centers, and automation systems. Services—the remaining 38% at $172 million—expanded 13% YoY, fueled by full-service maintenance contracts, field upgrades, and our rapidly scaling remote diagnostics offerings. Gross margins here remain stellar at 68%, compared to 28% for new equipment, contributing to our blended company margin expansion.

Key trends include the aging installed base of our equipment—our global fleet of over 1.2 million units now averages 8.5 years old, up from 7.8 years in 2022, creating a natural tailwind for replacement parts. Utilization rates across end-markets like mining, construction, and automotive OEMs have rebounded to 82%—the highest since pre-COVID—boosting consumables pull-through. We're seeing strong parts-per-unit economics: for every new excavator sold, we capture $15,000 in parts over the first five years, but for our legacy fleet—think Cat 793-class haulers or Komatsu-inspired dozers—that ramps to $45,000+ as uptime becomes mission-critical amid labor shortages.

Regionally, North America led with 22% YoY growth to $210 million, or 47% of aftermarket, propelled by U.S. infrastructure spending under the IIJA, including data center builds driving demand for our palletizers and AS/RS systems. EMEA grew 12% to $120 million, resilient despite softer German auto capex, thanks to wind farm O&M contracts. APAC shone at 14% growth to $95 million, or 21% of total, with China’s Made in China 2025 initiatives spurring upgrades in semiconductor fab equipment and India’s highway expansions pulling through bulldozer undercarriages. LatAm grew 8% but lagged due to mining slowdowns in Brazil; we're countering with localized service hubs.

Strategically, our Dyn telematics platform—now live on 65% of the active fleet, up from 45% last year—uses IoT sensors and AI-driven predictive maintenance to flag failures 72 hours in advance, reducing unplanned downtime by 28% for customers and lifting our contract attachment rate to 72%. We've rolled out digital twins for 40% of our high-volume parts, enabling virtual prototyping that cuts lead times from 12 weeks to 4, directly feeding parts velocity. Partnerships like our expanded alliance with Siemens for integrated PLC upgrades have secured $150 million in multi-year service deals, while our MRO distribution pact with Motion Industries ensures 98% fill rates on next-day parts delivery.

Looking forward, we see aftermarket growing 14-16% for FY24, pushing its revenue share toward 40%. This includes targeting $200 million in new service contract wins in H2 via TCO-focused pitches that lower customers' total ownership costs by 15-20% versus third-party alternatives. In a market where industrial capex remains lumpy—with ISM PMI at 49—this high-visibility stream de-risks our profile and supports 12-15% EPS growth.

Shifting to overall revenue performance by geographic region, which totaled $1.22 billion for the quarter—up 13% YoY and 7% on a constant currency basis, exceeding our guidance. This reflects strong volume growth from SmartFactory IoT platform integrations, modest pricing, and resilient demand amid supply chain reconfigurations. Our mix is diversified: North America 42%, EMEA 28%, Asia-Pacific 24%, Rest of World 6%.

North America, at 42% or $525 million, grew 15% YoY and 12% FX neutral, driven by reshoring and CHIPS Act-fueled semiconductor expansions. Robust bookings from hyperscalers and auto OEMs for our Viper Series CNC mills, with adaptive AI controls for 20% faster throughput on titanium and composites, included a $150 million multi-year contract with a major U.S. EV battery producer for automated electrode winding lines. Backlog hit $2.8 billion, up 18% YoY. Ohio and Texas factories ran at 92% utilization, with margins at 28% from localized sourcing.

EMEA, 28% or $350 million, rose 7% YoY and 10% FX neutral, tempered by energy volatility and softer German auto demand but led by UK and French aerospace aftermarket for AeroForge hydraulic presses aligning with Airbus and Safran ramp-ups. A €80 million deal with a Siemens-partnered wind turbine OEM for high-torque robotic welders capitalized on EU Green Deal subsidies. Our Hamburg demo center drove 15% trial-to-sale conversion.

Asia-Pacific, 24% or $300 million, surged 18% YoY and 16% FX neutral, fueled by China’s Made in China 2025 and India’s PLI scheme. Demand for QuantumFlex palletizers in consumer electronics from Foxconn and Samsung fabs totaled $100 million, with ASPs up 5%. Vietnam drew $40 million in transfer tooling. Edge-computing upgrades cut downtime 25% for semiconductor etchers, gaining 8% market share per Gartner.

Rest of World, 6% or $75 million, grew 5% YoY, with Brazil’s agribusiness boosting TerraGrip material handlers and Gulf oilfield services taking ruggedized CNCs.

Our revenue beat reflects Industry 4.0 monetization—40% tied to digital twins and remote diagnostics, ARR up 25% to $180 million—sustainability leadership with ISO 14001-certified lines, and supply chain agility keeping inventory at 75 days. For Q3, we guide $1.25-$1.29 billion, or 11-15% YoY growth.

Now, on operating margin performance by segment, which was a standout, with group adjusted operating margin expanding 210 basis points YoY to 15.4%—our strongest Q2 in five years. Excluding a $25 million gain from divesting our legacy hydraulic press line, core margin grew 140 basis points to 14.1%. This came from higher-margin aftermarket and electrification mix, 4.2% pricing, and $180 million in cost savings from lean initiatives and relocalization.

Construction & Mining Equipment, 45% of sales at $2.8 billion annualized pace, expanded 320 basis points to 13.2%, with 8% volume from IIJA and Australian mining, plus 5% pricing offsetting 12% steel costs. North America at 15.8%, EMEA 11.5%, APAC 12.9%. $300 million in autonomous haulage tech pilots with Rio Tinto targets 200 more basis points by FY25.

Powertrain & Engines, 25% at $1.5 billion pace, improved 180 basis points to 16.8%, with 6% organic sales, 4.5% pricing covering inflation, and PowerFlex redesign saving $45 million. North America 18.2% on data centers, Europe 14.5%, APAC 16.0%. Electrification JV with ABB secured $200 million orders.

Industrial Automation, 15% at $950 million pace, rose 250 basis points to 21.4%, with 11% sales from cobots and PLCs, 3.8% pricing, and SaaS shift. North America 23.1%, EMEA 20.2%, APAC 19.8%. SmartFactory 4.0 at 150 sites boosts throughput 10%.

Services & Parts, 15% at $900 million pace, gained 150 basis points to 28.7%, attach rates at 42%. FleetOptix with AR support lifts uptime 18%.

FX shaved 40 basis points, but non-U.S. revenue hedges it. Q3 margins guide 15.8-16.2%.

We are managing our capital allocation effectively. On share repurchases, in February our Board authorized a $2.5 billion open-market program, superseding the prior $1.8 billion fully exhausted by Q1. We've executed $1.9 billion, or 76%, retiring 22.4 million shares at $84.72 average. Q2 saw $650 million, 7.3 million shares at $89.15, reducing shares outstanding to 248.6 million from 265.4 million—a 6.4% drop delivering $0.28 EPS accretion and 8% tangible book value per share growth to $42.51.

Execution used VWAP algorithms with ML for volatility, targeting 15-20% discounts to DCF intrinsic value—11x EV/EBITDA for Construction vs. peers. North America drove 62% or $1.18 billion YTD on IIJA FCF $920 million up 18%. APAC 22% or $418 million on semiconductor capex. EMEA 16% or $302 million amid mining drops but EU Green Deal green shoots.

This prioritizes returns in maturing capex cycles, like peers CAT's $20 billion program. ROIC hit 14.2% from 12.8%, with $4.2 billion dry powder. $600 million remains; accelerate if below $85 on tariffs.

Finally, our dividend policy targets 40-50% payout of adjusted net income, with progressive growth tied to EPS. Annualized $3.20 per share, up 8% YoY, for 2.8% forward yield at $114—above S&P Industrials 1.7%, with 18-year raise streak at 7.5% CAGR. Payout at 42% Q2, FCF yield 5.2% covering 2.8x. North America appeals to pensions, Europe to Green Deal, APAC attractive post-hedging.

$850 million capex includes $200 million Industry 4.0. Guide 6-8% growth 2025 to 2.9-3.1% yield.

Next, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've been focused on improving productivity and efficiency across our manufacturing facilities. We've implemented lean manufacturing principles throughout our plants, leveraging data analytics to optimize processes from CNC machining to assembly lines. Supply chain resilience has been key—we've dual-sourced critical components like steel and semiconductors, reducing lead times by 25% and inventory days to 75 versus industry averages. Investments in workforce upskilling have also helped address labor challenges, with targeted training in automation and predictive maintenance boosting our technician retention by 18%. Utilization across facilities hit 88%, supporting margin gains.

And I would like to turn the call over to our CTO, David Kwon, for an update on our technology roadmap.

David Kwon (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers in the industrial equipment space. We're investing heavily in R&D in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things. Our Automation and Digital Solutions segment delivered $285 million in Q2 revenue, up 28% YoY and 15% sequentially—now 32% of total revenue, with SaaS recurring at $112 million up 42% and EBITDA margins at 29.7%, up 420 basis points from mix and cloud scale.

This rides Industry 4.0 tailwinds, with 12-15% CAGR per McKinsey/IDC. Book-to-bill 1.35x, ASPs up 8% on smart factory bundles. Our IndustroLink AI Platform, on 4,200+ sites up 35% YoY, uses edge analytics to cut downtime 27%—$10-15 million savings per steel mill or fab. OEE lifts from 72% to 88-92%, MTTR from 8 to 2 hours, throughput +18%. Magna-like auto supplier saw 22% OEE gain, $28 million productivity.

North America 48% of sales, +35% on reshoring, EdgeForge 2.1x book-to-bill. EMEA 28%, +22% on Green Deal energy savings 15-20%. APAC 24%, +25% on QuantumPredict cutting defects 14%.

$450 million FY24 capex on GenAI for recipes, VirtuFab digital twins cutting commissioning 40%, NVIDIA JV for edge, Komatsu retrofits. FY25 growth 25-30%, services 45%, margins +200-300 bps. Flywheel: sticky ARR 92% NRR, cross-sell.

Our new IndustroLink platform is showing promising early results, with significant impact on customer OEE and throughput. We believe these technologies will transform the industrial landscape and create significant opportunities for GIDC.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the growth drivers in your digital solutions business?

David Kwon (CTO):
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, our digital solutions are a core growth engine. As I mentioned, the Automation and Digital segment grew 28% YoY to $285 million, with SaaS at $112 million up 42%. Drivers include IndustroLink's deployment to 4,200 sites, delivering 27% downtime cuts and OEE to 88-92%. Regional strength in North America reshoring, EMEA Green Deal, and APAC fabs. Investments in GenAI, digital twins, and partnerships like NVIDIA position us for 25-30% FY25 growth. It's creating a flywheel with high retention and bundling.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen (Goldman Sachs):
What are your plans for expanding your presence in emerging markets?

John Ramirez (CEO):
Great question, Emily. Emerging markets, particularly APAC and LatAm, are key to our growth. In APAC, up 18% to $300 million, we're capitalizing on China's Made in China 2025 and India's PLI with palletizers and fab upgrades—backlog up 22%. Localized JVs and Singapore hubs navigate tariffs. LatAm grew 8% despite Brazil mining, with service hubs and agribusiness wins like TerraGrip handlers. Plans include $200 million capex for India expansions and bolt-ons in EV drivetrains. Backlog visibility supports 20%+ growth there.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you addressing the skilled labor shortage in the manufacturing sector?

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thanks, Tom. The skilled labor shortage is industry-wide, but we've tackled it head-on through workforce development. Our training programs in automation, IoT, and predictive maintenance have upskilled 2,500 technicians this year, improving retention 18%. Dyn telematics and AR remote support reduce reliance on on-site experts, cutting MTTR 75%. Partnerships with community colleges and incentives like tuition reimbursement fill gaps. This supports 88% facility utilization and positions us for electrification ramps.

John Ramirez (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson (VP of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
